findings.summary: Plan 26's production topology (runtime/langgraph_factory/graph.py, routing.py, unit_graph.py, repair.py, acceptance.py, workbook.py) was already correct and fully passing (209/209 across the four owned integration-test files) before this node's own changes -- this attempt's job was to prove and permanently encode that ownership, not to build the topology. A machine-readable ownership matrix (plans/27_langgraph_curriculum_factory_remediation/contracts/integration_ownership.v1.yaml, 75 claims) now checks, against real repository bytes rather than assertion: single, exclusive Run 27 ownership of all six modules and all four owned integration tests; every D-node body/registration-seam symbol this node is responsible for (build_curriculum_factory_graph, register_skeleton/register_unit_repair_topology/register_workbook_topology, binding_inventory family, validate_bindings; every route_* decision function; D16-D23's repair/acceptance bodies across repair.py/acceptance.py; D24-D32's workbook/release bodies across workbook.py); graph.py imports the shared node registry and never imports gemini; and no retired-provider credential name appears in any of the four owned tests. This contract is itself the 'ownership-closure check the scheduler can run before each future node attempt' the prompt's item 7 requires -- controller/verify_ownership.py (built by N10, reused unchanged here) is the generic, already-reusable engine; N40's contribution is authoring this node's own claims against it.

scan_node.py --node N40_INTEGRATION_OWNERSHIP genuinely failed on first real run: tests/runtime/test_plan26_topology.py's own forbidden-import guard (test_production_graph_imports_contain_no_fallback_controller) legitimately named the two retired Gemini-family import targets it asserts must be absent ("langchain_google_genai", "google.generativeai") as literal strings, which the blunt, non-semantic retired_provider_test_scan term scan cannot distinguish from an actual live reference. Per this node's own prompt ('Remove every retired-provider reference from its owned active topology test and keep the zero-occurrence test scan green'), the fix removes the retired provider's own name from the test and instead asserts absence by the shared module-name suffix common to that whole SDK family ("generativeai", "_genai") -- strictly broader (catches every fork of that SDK family, not just the two named ones), not weaker, and scan_node.py --node N40_INTEGRATION_OWNERSHIP now reports zero violations across all ten of this node's scanned files.
